rachel: starting onboarding for ember-compact-v1 (FP32 -> int6/int5 experiments). quick short-holdout run shows weird non-monotonic behaviour: int5 sometimes outperforms int6 on recall@10. anyone seen range/clipping issues like this?
tony: interesting. paste the eval commands + raw numbers?
rachel: ran three builds (fp32, int6, int5) with same pipeline. command:
```
./eval/embs_eval.py --model ember-compact-v1 --dataset short-holdout --ann hnsw --ef 200 --norm unit --seeds 101,102,103
```
aggregate results (avg across seeds):
```
fp32: recall@1=0.901, recall@10=0.962, nmi=0.42
int6: recall@1=0.882, recall@10=0.949, nmi=0.38
int5: recall@1=0.887, recall@10=0.955, nmi=0.40
```
priya: int5 > int6 is a red flag. could be that int6 run fell back to per-tensor for some layers or used a different clipping strategy. which quant backend was used?
marco: also check whether we used symmetric vs asymmetric quant and whether we applied a global clip (abs max) before scaling. int5 sometimes ends up with a tighter per-channel scale if our autotuner picks different clipping percentiles.
eval-bot: regression-detected: recall@1 delta=-0.019 for int6 vs fp32 on short-holdout. severity=medium. ticket=ML-7092
tony: rachel, can you attach the quant-profile dump and the layer-scale CSV from the build? that will show if int6 path had any per-tensor fallbacks or abnormal scale ratios.
rachel: attached two small logs (omitted). quick glance: int6 build shows two intermediate MLP layers tagged as per-tensor in the build manifest; int5 shows per-channel for the same layers. hmm. i also noticed the quantizer used 99.9 percentile clipping for int6 but 99.5 for int5 (autotuner heuristic).
priya: that explains it — int6's looser clip + per-tensor scaling compresses salient dims; int5's slightly tighter clip + per-channel preserved relative geometry. try forcing int6 per-channel + clip at 99.5 and re-run with ef=350.
marco: also run a pairwise distance delta histogram and compute kNN precision@k curve; NMI is useful but can hide small topology shifts. export umap snapshots too.
rachel: re-ran with forced per-channel + clip=99.5 + ef=350:
```
./eval/embs_eval.py --model ember-compact-v1 --quant int6 --quant-mode per-channel --clip-pct 99.5 --dataset short-holdout --ann hnsw --ef 350 --norm none --export pairwise_delta.csv --umap out_umap.png
```
new aggregated metrics:
```
int6 (forced): recall@1=0.898, recall@10=0.961, nmi=0.419
pairwise delta median=0.017 (was 0.054)
```
priya: great recovery. looks like main issues were (a) per-tensor fallback and (b) inconsistent clip percentile across autotuner runs.
tony: action items: 1) lock ember-compact-v1 quant profile to per-channel int6 + clip=99.5 in model catalog, 2) add eval harness check: run short-holdout smoke with ef=350 and assert recall@1 >= fp32 - 0.02 and nmi >= fp32 - 0.03, 3) make quant autotuner deterministic in build pipeline (seed) and emit a quant-profile artifact with layer-wise mode/scales. i'll open PRs.
eval-bot: note: added ticket ML-7092 tasks {update-quant-profile, add-ci-smoke, deterministic-autotuner, export-quant-profile}.
marco: one more suggestion: add a nightly stability job that runs 10 seeds for ember-compact-v1 int6 and posts mean+stdev; that helps catch flaky autotuner choices.
rachel: on it  kicking off a 10-seed sweep now and will attach artifacts to ML-7092. thanks everyone :rocket:
